title.english: Publisher's note to the Chowkhamba reprint

components.evidence: csldoc vcppref04 scan viewed 24-09-2026: English note praising the encyclopaedic scope (Vedas to Vastushastra; sixteen philosophy systems), claiming additions beyond Wilson's Dictionary, Radhakanta's Shabdakalpadruma and Böhtlingk's St. Petersburg dictionary, and explaining the reprint motive; carries a University of Toronto library stamp (AUG 17 1964) and accession number 920660.

title.asPrinted: THIS WORK IS DEDICATED TO HIS HIGHNESS SREE MAHARAJAH MEERZA ANANDA GAJAPATTI RAJ MUNEERA SULTAN BAHADOOR OF VIZIANAGARAM
title.english: Dedication to the Maharaja of Vizianagaram, patron of Sanskrit learning

components.evidence: csldoc vcppref05 scan viewed 24-09-2026: dedication 'in acknowledgement of the deep interest shewn by His Highness for the advancement of Sanskrit learning, and of the liberal patronage afforded to the cause of Sanskrit language by the ancestors of His Highness', signed 'Taranatha Tarkavachaspati, the Author'.

title.english: Preface by H. Woodrow on the making and patronage of the dictionary

components.evidence: csldoc vcppref06 scan viewed 24-09-2026: signed 'H. Woodrow, M.A., Inspector of Schools, Lower provinces of Bengal'; records Taranatha's Panini edition of 1863, the Government of Bengal patronage (letter No. 507, Fort William, 25th January 1866: 200 copies at Rs 50), the five-year extension (letter No. 3480, 12th December 1870), and the aim to exceed Wilson's Dictionary and the Shabdakalpadruma with Sanskrit explanations.
components.notes: A sponsor's preface, not the author's; names the bilingual purpose 'for the use of both Hindu and European scholars'.

title.english: Contents: the seventeen subjects the dictionary undertakes to cover

decodes.markup: gender marks (m./f./n.) and derivations inside vcp.txt entries
decodes.mechanism: items 1-3 announce the Paninian apparatus: genders, suffixes, primitive and derivative words.

components.evidence: csldoc vcppref07 scan viewed 24-09-2026: seventeen numbered items, from 'Panini on genders', 'On the suffixes', 'On the primitive and derivative words' and the derivations drawn from Wilson's Dictionary and Radhakanta's Shabdakalpadruma, through Vaidik words, Śrauta and Gṛihya sūtra terms, philosophy systems, Hindu law, Puranas, Ramayana, ancient kings, geography, medicine, astronomy, astrology, and the technical words of the Tantras, politics, rhetoric, prosody, music, military science, cookery, Siksha, Kalpa, horses, Hatyoga and Vastushastra, to the classification of the Vedas.

components.componentTypeNote: An authorial treatise printed ahead of the letter A, not a display key: recorded as an embedded text that decodes the dictionary's grammatical notation.

title.english: Taranatha's own Sanskrit grammatical introduction: the Liṅgānuśāsana with its verse paricchiṣṭa (printed pp. 1-34 of vol. 1)

decodes.target: gender assignment and suffix derivation behind the entries
decodes.markup: gender marks and derivational explanations in vcp.txt entries (Contents items 1-3)
decodes.mechanism: the treatise argues the Paninian doctrine of genders ( prati-grahya linga-visesanani ) and of primitive and derivative words that the entries apply; Taranatha cites sutra-by-sutra.

components.evidence: All 34 VCPScan pages fetched and viewed 24-09-2026 (contact sheets; key pages at full resolution): opens 'प्रतिग्रह्यं लिङ्गविशेषणानामेव ... पाणिनीयमतम् सुदृढम्' with numbered rule-discussions (स्त्री 1, क्लिबं 5, स्त्रीप्रत्ययान्ताः षट् 7, ...), continues through gender-word lists and the 'शब्दविभागविचार' prose, and closes with the colophon naming the Liṅgānuśāsana of the Śabdārthacintāmaṇi ('इति श्रीमच्छब्दार्थचिन्तामणौ ... लिङ्गानुशासनम्') followed by the verse paricchiṣṭa ('परिशिष्ट इत्येष प्रबन्धः') and benediction verses; printed Devanagari page numbers १-३४ seen on the viewed leaves.
components.notes: Internal section boundaries (liṅga rules, word lists, vibhaga-vicara, paricchiṣṭa) were classified from the viewed pages but not itemised page by page.
